messages:
sam: Quick sync 999We need to decide service auth architecture: pure gateway RBAC (Envoy) vs external policy agent (OPA) vs hybrid. Short pros/cons?

lina: Gateway = single enforcement point, simple for ingress, lower latencies. OPA = expressive policies, versioned bundles, but external calls and more surface area.

derek: Gateway-only added <15ms p95 on our test; adding a remote OPA added ~20ms p95. For high-throughput paths, that matters.

maya: OPA wins on expressiveness: hierarchical org/project rules, attribute-based decisions, easier to canary policy changes.

sam: Thinking about decision factors: latency, failure modes, expressiveness, rollout/CI, telemetry, dev ergonomics. Anything else?

lina: Authoring surface: if we pick OPA, teams can push policy bundles (sidecar/local). If gateway, teams need central PRs or a policy API. Ops burden differs.

derek: Failure modes matter: gateway-down can be global outage. OPA-down could be per-service degradation. Need clear fallback semantics.

maya: Hybrid pattern idea: coarse-grained checks (token validity, org/project claim, route allow) in gateway; fine-grained attribute checks via local OPA sidecars for services that need it.

sam: Sketch: 1) Gateway validates token, enforces coarse RBAC (roles, route allow). 2) Services run local OPA sidecar for fine grained ABAC; sidecars get bundles from central registry. 3) Central policy CI and bundle signing.

lina: Fallback policy: if sidecar unreachable, what then? deny-by-default breaks apps. Maybe gateway allows when coarse check passes but marks request for audit when fine-grain unavailable.

derek: We should risk-classify endpoints: HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW. Default fallback per bucket: HIGH -> deny on missing fine-grain, MEDIUM -> allow+alert, LOW -> allow.

maya: Example mapping: admin APIs -> HIGH, billing/thresholding -> MEDIUM, read-only public-ish -> LOW. We'll produce a mapping.

sam: Ops question: sidecars add memory/ops cost. Central OPA cluster reduces pods but needs caching and increases request hops. Tradeoff notes?

lina: Sidecars = local eval, predictable perf, more memory. Centralized = simpler ops footprint, caching layer required, single failure domain. Either ok if we provide tooling for bundle distribution and rollout.

derek: Telemetry: gateway must emit token verification outcomes, coarse decision tags, latency. OPA decisions include policy bundle id and rule id to trace regressions.

maya: Migration for API keys & RBAC: plan: 1) export key->role mappings, 2) augment tokens with org/project claims for a trial, 3) run policies in shadow mode 2wks, compare denies, 4) enable progressive deny-by-default.

sam: Token scoping debate: project-scoped short-lived keys vs org-wide long-lived tokens. Ops wants fewer tokens, product wants per-product scoping. Proposed default: project-scoped keys, org-scoped only via approval with shorter TTL and stronger audit.

lina: Migration shim: accept legacy keys at edge, mint short-lived claim-bearing internal tokens (kid header) and forward to services. That keeps internal auth simple.

derek: Perf task: I'll run microbenchmarks: gateway-only vs gateway+sidecar vs gateway+central-opa on friday.

maya: Policy rollout: CI -> policy lint -> staging bundle -> canary 5% -> 100%. Shadow mode for 2wks before enforce.

sam: Need RFC doc: include architecture diagram, decision matrix, fallback defaults per risk bucket, rollout plan, metrics. Lina to draft RFC. Action items: Lina draft by EOD Thu; Derek perf on Fri; Maya to produce risk bucket mapping; Sam to define telemetry schema.

security-bot: Reminder: run automated policy linter and reachability tests before enabling deny-by-default.

derek: +1. Also include bundle signing and enforced bundle version tagging in telemetry.

maya: A few open Qs: how do teams author rules? Git-first bundles? UI? who owns central registry? We should propose a simple gitops flow first.

lina: Agree: gitops for now, CI validation, then explore a web UI later. Maintain a policy-owner list per bundle.

sam: TL;DR: go hybrid: gateway coarse-grain + local policy for fine-grain. Risk-bucket fallback semantics. Default project-first key policy with approved org tokens. Shadow-run before enforcement. RFC incoming. Ping Lina to review.
